steps.title: Get Docker
steps.body: Docker Desktop on Windows or macOS, Docker Engine on Linux.

steps.title: Start Agentivity
steps.body: One command. Your data is kept in a Docker volume, so it survives a restart or an update.

steps.title: Open the Studio
steps.body: In your browser, on the machine where it runs:

steps.title: Connect an AI model
steps.body: Add the key of the provider you use: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, xAI or AWS Bedrock. Then create your first agent and run it.

items.title: There is no login yet
items.body: Anyone who can reach the server can use it. Keep it on a network you trust, or behind your own access control. Never expose it directly to the internet.

items.title: Your data stays with you
items.body: Agents, teams, workflows, tables and settings are stored in the agentivity-data volume. Back it up like any other data. What you send in an AI step goes to the model provider you chose.

items.title: Updating
items.body: Pull the new image, remove the container and start it again with the same command. The volume keeps your data.
items.command: docker pull agentivitylabs/agentivity && docker rm -f agentivity

items.body: One web page where your colleagues start the teams you have published, under your brand. Nothing to develop.

items.title: A VibeApp
items.body: An app of your own, with one or several of your teams behind it. Most VibeApps mix classic screens and teams.

showcases.sub: Each one has its page: what happens, who decides, and the team behind it.

examples: One sentence: Lisbon for two, the dates, the budget.
The manager calls in the specialists this trip needs: flights, hotel, transfers, dinner.
What the traveller chooses changes what comes next: dinner fits what is left of the budget.

soon.h2_accent: Two of them need no app.
soon.sub: They run on the server and reach you where you already work.

items.title: Supplier invoices
items.body: The team reads the invoice mailbox, checks every figure, spots duplicates and reminders, and asks the accountant to validate the doubtful ones by email or Slack.

items.title: Quote requests
items.for: an independent or a small business
items.body: A customer fills in a form. The team prepares the quote, the owner approves or corrects it from their inbox, and the answer goes out.

items.title: Sport and nutrition coach
items.body: A personal app: training and meals planned around your goals, and adjusted week after week.

soon.link: Tell me when they are out

cases.title: Trip Planner
cases.summary: One sentence in. A manager and twelve specialists plan the trip, and the traveller chooses the flights, the hotel and the dinner.
cases.alt: A recording of the Trip Planner app: a traveller asks for a trip to Lisbon, a manager hands the work to specialists, and the app asks the traveller to choose the flights, the hotel, the transfers and the dinner
cases.lead: The traveller writes what they want. A manager hands each part to the right specialist, and the app shows a choice each time a decision belongs to the traveller.

facts.for: A travel agency, or anyone who sells something with many parts
facts.use: A VibeApp, made for this one job

steps.title: The request
steps.body: One sentence: Lisbon for two, the dates, the budget.

steps.title: The manager takes it
steps.body: It splits the trip and hands each part to the right specialist.

steps.title: The specialists propose
steps.body: Flights, hotel, transfers, dinner: each one comes back with options that fit the budget.

steps.title: The traveller chooses
steps.body: The app shows a card for each choice, with photos and prices.

steps.title: Payment, then reservations
steps.body: Once the payment is authorised, one member confirms every reservation.

team.title: The team
team.lead: Thirteen members. Only the manager talks to all the others.

members.name: Trip Manager
members.role: Coordinates the specialists and keeps the trip coherent.

members.name: Flight Specialist
members.role: Proposes the flights.

members.name: Hotel Specialist
members.role: Proposes the hotel that fits best.

members.name: Ground Transport Specialist
members.role: Proposes airport transfers and local transport.

members.name: Car Rental Specialist
members.role: Proposes a rental car when it makes sense.

members.name: Restaurant & Dining Specialist
members.role: Recommends restaurants.

members.name: Activity Planner
members.role: Builds a day-by-day programme around the traveller’s interests.

members.name: Travel Insurance Specialist
members.role: Proposes an insurance policy.

members.name: Visa & Documents Specialist
members.role: Checks visa, passport and vaccination requirements.

members.name: Currency & Budget Advisor
members.role: Advises on currency and checks the budget across the specialists.

members.name: Payment Agent
members.role: Handles the payment and reports whether it was authorised.

members.name: Reservation Agent
members.role: Confirms every reservation once the payment is authorised.

members.name: On-Trip Assistant
members.role: Handles changes once the trip is confirmed.

cases.note: This is a demonstration. Flights, hotels and payment are simulated: nothing is really booked or charged.

get.body: The code of the app is public. It needs the AI teams of the Community edition.

cases.title: Shopping Lab
cases.for: a shop, a buyer, a comparison service
cases.summary: A shopper describes what they need. Nine specialists read the stores’ own pages, compare, score and write an illustrated report.
cases.alt: A recording of the Shopping Lab demo in the portal: a shopper asks for headphones, nine specialists work in turn, then a report with product cards and photos appears
cases.lead: The shopper describes a need in their own words. The team reads what the stores really publish, compares like with like, and hands back a report with its sources.

facts.for: A shop, a purchasing department, a comparison service
facts.use: The ready-made portal, with no app to build

steps.title: The need
steps.body: A vague wish becomes a precise brief: product, budget, must-haves, priorities.

steps.title: The stores
steps.body: One scout per store reads its pages: real prices, ratings, reviews, photos and specifications.

steps.title: The comparison
steps.body: The same product is merged across stores, and the specifications are put in common units.

steps.title: The score
steps.body: Each product is scored by a fixed calculation, never by estimation.

steps.title: The report
steps.body: A verdict, the top picks with photos, charts, the points to watch and the sources.

decisions: Confirm the brief before the search starts
Read the report and decide what to buy

team.title: The team
team.lead: Nine members. Only one of them talks to the shopper.

members.name: Needs Analyst
members.role: Turns a vague wish into a precise, confirmed brief. The only member who talks to the shopper.

members.name: Query Planner
members.role: Prepares the search for each store from the confirmed brief.

members.name: Store Scouts (2)
members.role: Each one reads one store’s own pages and reports prices, ratings, reviews, photos and specifications.

members.name: Product Matcher
members.role: Merges the same product across stores and keeps the best offer of each.

members.name: Spec Normalizer
members.role: Builds a clean side-by-side comparison. Never fills a gap with a guess.

members.name: Scoring Analyst
members.role: Scores every product with a fixed calculation.

members.name: Customer Reviews Analyst
members.role: Says what customers really think, and where to be careful.

members.name: Report Writer
members.role: Writes the final illustrated report.

cases.note: The demonstration reads two online stores. Add a scout, and the team covers another one.

cases.title: CV Screening
cases.summary: A CV and a job description in. A score, the reasons, and a route: shortlist, rejection, or review by a recruiter.
cases.alt: A recording of the Studio showing the CV Screening workflow: boxes for reading the file, reading the page, assessing the fit and asking a person, linked from left to right
cases.lead: The recruiter gives a CV and a job description. The workflow reads both, scores the fit, explains why, and sends the doubtful cases to a person.

facts.for: A recruiter or an HR team
facts.use: A form to drop the CV, and the result on screen
facts.behind: A workflow of 34 steps, drawn in the Studio

steps.title: The documents
steps.body: The CV and the job description, each as a file, a link or plain text.

steps.title: The reading
steps.body: The workflow extracts the text of the file or reads the web page. If it cannot, it asks a person.

steps.title: The assessment
steps.body: It scores the fit and brings out seniority and career signals.

steps.title: The route
steps.body: Shortlist, rejection, or review by a recruiter.

decisions: Help when a document cannot be read
Review the cases the workflow is not sure about

team.title: The building blocks
team.lead: A workflow is drawn box by box. These are the kinds of boxes this one uses.

members.name: Form
members.role: Where the recruiter drops the CV and the job description.

members.name: Read the file
members.role: Extracts the text of a document.

members.name: Read the page
members.role: Reads a job description published on the web.

members.name: AI steps
members.role: Assess the fit and write the reasons.

members.name: Conditions
members.role: Send each case down the right route.

members.name: Human steps
members.role: Stop and wait for a person when one is needed.

cases.note: A workflow follows the path you drew, the same way every time. A team decides its own path. You can mix both.
